en.title: Mode of Digital Roots After Repeated Digit Sums
en.description: You are given a list of digit strings. For each value, repeatedly sum its digits until a single digit remains; return the mode, the single digit that occurs most frequently. On a tie, this site returns the larger digital root.
en.input: The first line contains N (this site limits 1≤N≤200000), followed by N lines, each containing a non-negative decimal digit string. Leading zeros are allowed; signs are not. Each string has length ≤100000, and the total number of digits is ≤2000000.
en.output: Output the mode; if several digital roots share the highest frequency, output the largest of them.
en.explanation: Scan the digits, sum them, and take the digital root modulo 9, then count the frequencies; zero maps to 0 separately.
hints: The digital root can be computed from the digit sum modulo 9.
A string of all zeros has digital root 0.
When the mode is tied, take the larger value per this site's rule.
